fixes.explanation: Nope, nothing about Egypt in this view. The LORD shows Moses the land, from Gilead as far as Dan, and all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea (Deuteronomy 34:1-2). The text says nothing about a road back to Egypt, friend. What He shows Moses is the land itself.

Right, baker. The LORD says, "I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross into it." (Deuteronomy 34:4) So the seeing is true, and the crossing is the part that's not happening. Moses gets the view, and he doesn't walk in.

Yes, friend. The text says, "And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab facing Beth-peor…" (Deuteronomy 34:6). The "He" there is the LORD. Moses is called the servant of the LORD (Deuteronomy 34:5), and the LORD Himself buries him. I think that's tender.

Eleazar, Aaron's son and a priest (Numbers 20:28), is a fair guess, but the passage doesn't name him here. The text says, "And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab facing Beth-peor…" (Deuteronomy 34:6). The "He" is the LORD.

That's right, baker. The valley facing Beth-peor part is true, but the text says, "…and no one to this day knows the location of his grave." (Deuteronomy 34:6) So nobody knew exactly where he was buried. Even I can lose a whole batch of cookies in my own bakery, but this is a grave, so I'll just say it plainly: the place isn't known.

You've got the strength part, but the eyes are the catch. The text says, "…yet his eyes were not weak, and his vitality had not diminished." (Deuteronomy 34:7) So his eyes weren't weak either. At a hundred and twenty, that's a surprise, friend.

Seven days is a fair guess, friend. But here the text says the Israelites grieved "…thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end." (Deuteronomy 34:8) So they gave it a lot longer than a week.

A mountain does show up in this passage, but it's Moses who climbs it (Deuteronomy 34:1). The reason the text gives for Joshua is that "…Moses had laid his hands on him." (Deuteronomy 34:9) Fasting isn't mentioned for Joshua here, friend.
Yes, baker. The text says, "So the Israelites obeyed him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Deuteronomy 34:9) They obeyed Joshua, and in doing it they did what the LORD had commanded Moses.

No resisting here, baker. The text says, "So the Israelites obeyed him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Deuteronomy 34:9) They obeyed Joshua, son of Nun, the one filled with the spirit of wisdom.

Think back to the start, friend. The LORD told Moses, "I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross into it." (Deuteronomy 34:4) But that isn't what the passage says sets Moses apart. It says he was the prophet "…whom the LORD knew face to face…" (Deuteronomy 34:10)

This one is true, baker. The text says no prophet performed "…all the mighty acts of power and awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel." (Deuteronomy 34:12) Everything on the card matches the verse. Moses did those deeds in the sight of all Israel.
